agent_notes: The whole psalm turns on who the second 'elohim' are. The Hebrew has the same word three times: 'elohim' (singular verb: God) standing in the 'adat-'el, judging in the midst of 'elohim' (plural: gods). I read the setting as the divine council (compare Ps 89:7), as most modern scholars do; Ibn Ezra, Rashi, Radak, Meiri, Metzudat David and Malbim take the plural elohim as human judges (or angels, in Ibn Ezra). I kept the literal layer ambiguous-neutral ('gods') and said in the commentary that the sense of the psalm is that the beings addressed are, or are treated as, divine. The KJV 'the mighty' for 'el is a harmonizing choice; ASV 'congregation of God' is closer.
Gloss 3 and 8: STEPBible glosses #3 'God' and #8 '[the] gods'. I keep that distinction. Gloss 6 'El' is STEPBible 'God' tagged to deity.yhwh; I read it as the divine name El, 'the assembly of El'.

Verse numbering: the Hebrew counts the superscription as verse 1, so the KJV's 82:0 and 82:1 are both inside this verse. Every later verse is one ahead of the KJV in the packet only in the sense that the packet's KJV column is aligned to it.
